ResStock assigns each dwelling unit a set of building characteristics. This includes attic type, insulation level, and climate zone by using probabilistic sampling logic informed by national housing stock data. Attic floor insulation is modeled as R- value for the ceiling assembly. These values reflect insulation material installed between and/or over the attic floor joists in unfinished, vented attic spaces. This modeling assumes that insulation is installed uniformly across the attic floor and that the attic remains unconditioned and vented. Attic insulation performance is influenced by the insulation material and its installed thickness, both of which determine the R-value. However, ResStock does not explicitly model material types; it focuses instead on the total thermal resistance for the entire assembly. Electrical panel constraint modeling was added to ResStock via OpenStudio-HPXML measures in 2025 to assess whether the existing panel has enough capacity or breaker space to accommodate new loads from an energy retrofit. For details on panel constraint modeling, refer to the ResStock Technical Reference Guide [1]. Attic floor insulation does not introduce new electrical loads or circuits, so they have no impact on the electrical panel. However, electrical panel metrics are included as a standard output for this and all other envelope measures. Any panel constraints appearing in the upgrade results reflect pre-existing conditions, as this measure does not worsen them. 3.1 OpenStudio-HPXML Overview The ResStock building stock energy model contains conditional probability distributions of building characteristics that are representative of the contiguous U.S. residential building stock. These are sampled to create a synthetic stock where each sample has an assigned option for each characteristic for each dwelling unit to be simulated. ResStock utilizes the OpenStudio-HPXML workflow to translate these dwelling characteristics into building models ready to be simulated via OpenStudio® and EnergyPlus® through the use of an HPXML file. For reference, the state of the OpenStudio-HPXML repository when the ResStock 2024 Release 2 dataset was created can be found here. Assumptions about the attic floor insulation upgrades that are not explicitly defined in ResStock are taken care of in the BuildResidentialHPXML measure. 3.2 Attic Floor Insulation In ResStock, building characteristics are translated to OS-HPXML parameters using the options_lookup.tsv file. Measure upgrades, such as ceiling insulation or attic floor insulation for unfinished attics, are modeled as changes to baseline building characteristics. This section outlines the technical details of how ceiling insulation upgrades are implemented in the ResStock workflow.
